sources.text:
# Library of Congress Migrant Mother collection guide

Source: https://guides.loc.gov/migrant-mother
Retrieved: 2026-10-11T13:39:42.197464+00:00

The photograph that has become known as "Migrant Mother" is one of a series of photographs that Dorothea Lange made of Florence Owens Thompson and her children in March of 1936 in Nipomo, California. Lange was concluding a month's trip photographing migratory farm labor around the state for what was then the Resettlement Administration.

# Library of Congress Dorothea Lange profile excerpt

Source: https://www.loc.gov/exhibits/wcf/wcf0013.html
Retrieved: 2026-10-11T13:41:42.629556+00:00

Like Esther Bubley, Dorothea Lange (1895-1965) documented the change on the homefront, especially among ethnic groups and workers uprooted by the war. Three months after Pearl Harbor, President Franklin Roosevelt ordered the relocation of Japanese-Americans into armed camps in the West. Soon after, the War Relocation Authority hired Lange to photograph Japanese neighborhoods, processing centers, and camp facilities.

# National Archives WRA administrative history excerpt

Source: https://www.archives.gov/research/guide-fed-records/groups/210.html
Retrieved: 2026-10-11T13:41:45.253401+00:00

Records of the War Relocation Authority [WRA]

Established: In the Office for Emergency Management by EO 9102, March 18, 1942. Predecessor Agencies: Wartime Civil Control Administration (WCCA), Western Defense Command (1942) Transfers: To the Department of the Interior by EO 9423, February 16, 1944.
